coordinate_semantics: footprint anchor x/y, y-up; not bbox centre
placeholder_note: Placeholders are <name>; every command is run as an argv list (never a shell string).

verify: --out file exists and parses as a JSON object
capture.identityVerified is true when a capture block is present
dump.status: documented and used by both round9 cases
dump.notes: Real CLI writes the dump to --out and may print the success line to stderr, so a non-JSON stdout is not a dump failure. PCB must be the foreground document; run doc switch first. Availability categories are read one by one; a missing bbox/pad/copper makes the dump incomplete, never silently signed.

save.notes: checkpoint:true only marks a journal entry; it never saves. A save that does not confirm saved:true must stop the save/reload proof.

reload.status: documented; receipt fields come from the predecessor v1.14 source and must be re-checked with `easycirq <cmd> --help` + `easycirq capabilities`
reload.notes: doc reload saves first, closes the tab and reopens it; it refreshes the per-document enumeration cache. Without it, DRC/check/readback evidence may be stale. Take a fresh dump after the reload and diff it against the pre-reload dump.

drc.status: documented and live-used (passed:true/total:0 in both cases)
drc.notes: The native DRC canvas recompute only finishes with the PCB window in the foreground; a background window times out and must not be retried in a loop. The command exits non-zero when passed:false or the result is inconclusive. Always capture the raw JSON, and run it after the final save/reload (a pre-reload DRC cannot claim final evidence).

verify: every WARN/INFO has a disposition entry
coverage/incomplete is reported, not assumed complete
check.status: documented and live-used (0 ERROR with 6/13 WARN in the two cases)
check.notes: passed:false may mean warnings only; never gate on the boolean alone. Gate on errors plus a disposition file. --strict turns any WARN/ERROR into a non-zero exit and is not used by the case recorder.

verify: score and crossingCount captured as measured
layout-lint.status: documented template; round9 case evidence was missing (scratch only); round10 live regression lint is in docs/round10/regression/liveA|liveB/evidence
layout-lint.notes: Score/crossings are placement quality, not routing correctness. Coverage incomplete is unmeasured and must not be reported as a pass. Run it after the final dump so the gate can prove it is fresh.

net-path.status: documented; both cases used per-pair scratch loops
net-path.notes: One call per required DESIGNATOR.PAD pair; the aggregate keeps each argv. Same net name is not connectivity. Pours, fills and PLANE copper are excluded from net-path; GND/power pours need native DRC plus poured-list evidence.

sch-read.notes: The schematic must be the active document: doc switch <schematic> before sch read, switch back to the PCB afterwards. Fallback is sch list --include-pins --project <project> --json. Comparison is exact designator+pad-number; combination pads need an explicit alias map instead of being guessed.

verify: PNG signature and positive IHDR width/height
stage-snapshot.status: documented; command existence is probed with --help
stage-snapshot.notes: Switch the canvas first with easycirq pcb view-side --side <top|bottom>. When stage-snapshot is unavailable, fall back to easycirq pcb snapshot --fit-mode board. Copy the reported artifact into the case instead of referencing .easycirq/artifacts, so the manifest hash travels with the case.

verify: metadata.sourceSha256 equals the sha256 of the measured dump
layout-render.status: documented and used by both cases (metadata.sourceSha256 verified)
layout-render.notes: Offline actual-geometry aid rendered from the dump; it is not an object-level official fabrication export. A sourceSha256 that does not match the final dump is a stale-binding failure.

verify: Supplier Part / MPN columns inspected separately
bom-export.status: documented; bom export has no --out and the artifact path comes from the receipt
bom-export.notes: bom export reads the active schematic; switch to the schematic and back to the PCB. --enrich=false keeps the raw export so an enrichment TypeError cannot fail an otherwise valid BOM; C-number enrichment and sourcing checks are a separate step. There is no --out flag: take the path from result.artifacts[].path.

project-export.status: documented and live-used (three archives in round9)
project-export.notes: The command refuses to overwrite an existing file; the case recorder checks existence first and never overwrites. An earlier case saw 'explicit --window and --project-uuid are required', so pass the measured capture.windowId when it is known. zipIntegrityVerified only proves the container; restoreVerified needs a separate reopen drill.

apply.notes: The playbook is a strict sequential queue (action | run | notify) with retry:0 for writes and continueOnError:false. --yes is only for an explicitly authorized confirm step. Save is a real pcb.save step; checkpoint:true never saves. Reload is run doc reload <doc> --json after the save.

verify: exit 0 for pass/pass_with_gaps, 1 for fail/blocked, 2 for input errors
gate.status: contract-defined; pcb_gate.py is Agent G's deliverable and may be absent while other agents work
gate.notes: pcb_case invokes it only when the script exists and --no-gate is not set. Its report status is copied into manifest.gate and re-checked by verification. The gate is read-only over the case directory.

case.notes: Live mode runs dump -> save-reload (final dump) -> checks -> images/bom/archive -> gate. --skip-live only assembles and verifies an existing case directory and never calls easycirq. A missing required artifact is not_run; an invalid or failed one is a failure. All writes stay inside the case directory, and the default archive is never overwritten. When --warn-disposition/--key-nets are omitted, evidence/warn-disposition.json and evidence/key-nets.json are auto-discovered from the case.

verify: after delete, pcb list --include-pads no longer contains the deleted component ids
delete.status: documented (components only); re-check argv with easycirq pcb delete --help
delete.notes: Delete accepts components only; passing a track/via id is refused (PRECONDITION_REFUSED). For single copper objects use track-delete / via-delete; for a whole net use rip-up --net.

verify: after delete, track-list no longer contains the deleted ids
track-delete.status: documented; re-check argv with easycirq pcb track-delete --help
track-delete.notes: Single track segments only. Whole-net removal uses rip-up --net, not repeated track-delete.

verify: after delete, via-list no longer contains the deleted ids
via-delete.status: documented; re-check argv with easycirq pcb via-delete --help

verify: after rip-up, track-list / via-list show no objects of the net
rip-up.status: documented; re-check argv with easycirq pcb rip-up --help
rip-up.notes: Whole-net removal. Scope to the exact net; never used to blanket-clear the board.

pour-rebuild.status: documented; re-check argv with easycirq pcb pour-rebuild --help
pour-rebuild.notes: After any copper change: apply -> pour-rebuild -> save -> doc reload -> DRC. A DRC run without a pour rebuild is invalid (fake spikes, see agent-collaboration.md).

verify: pcb drc-rules reads back the written values
pre-routing and final drc-rules archived by pcb_case
drc-rules-set.status: documented; re-check argv with easycirq pcb drc-rules-set --help
drc-rules-set.notes: Record the rules before routing. Never silently relax rules to clear DRC; a relaxation needs a decision/waiver record.

verify: ids used by the plan exist after apply / are gone after track-delete
track-list.status: documented; re-check argv with easycirq pcb track-list --help
track-list.notes: Readback for placed tracks; used to confirm delete and to detect timeout residue.

verify: ids used by the plan exist after apply / are gone after via-delete
via-list.status: documented; re-check argv with easycirq pcb via-list --help
via-list.notes: Readback for placed vias (incl. stitch vias).

pour-list.status: documented; re-check argv with easycirq pcb pour-list --help
pour-list.notes: Readback for copper pours; poured-list is the rebuilt-materialization view.

doc-switch.notes: Needed before every PCB command (PCB foreground) and before bom export (schematic foreground). Switch back to the PCB afterwards.

doc-ls.notes: Used when the schematic document name/uuid is not supplied. Parse defensively: look for a document whose type is schematic/sch rather than guessing from position.

snapshot-fallback.notes: Used only when pcb stage-snapshot --help fails. The resulting PNG is a viewport snapshot, not an object-level export.

pcb-dump-before.description: fresh measured dump before the save/reload proof

pcb-dump-after-reload.description: fresh measured dump after save + doc reload; the final dump

pcb-dump-final.description: measured dump used when no dedicated before/reload dump exists

save-reload-diff.description: diff_boards(before, after); match is required for persistence

pcb-drc.description: raw native DRC JSON; passed:true and total:0

pcb-check.description: raw pcb check JSON; 0 ERROR plus WARN dispositions

netpath-key-connections.description: aggregated per-pair net-path rows with per-row argv

image-top.description: top PNG copied into the case

image-bottom.description: bottom PNG copied into the case

actual-svg.description: layout render --actual SVG bound by metadata.sourceSha256

bom.description: raw --enrich=false CSV copied into the case
